q: In a class of 40 students, Ravi ranks 16th from the top. What is his rank from the bottom?
exp: Rank from bottom = 40−16+1 = 25.

q: In a row of 35 students, Neha ranks 12th from the left. What is her rank from the right?
exp: Rank from right = 35−12+1 = 24.

q: In a class, Aman is 9th from the top and 22nd from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
exp: Total students = 9+22−1 = 30.

q: In a row of 50 people, Kiran is 18th from the left. How many people are to her right?
exp: People to the right = 50−18 = 32.

q: In a row of 28 students, Priya is 7th from the right. What is her position from the left?
exp: Position from left = 28−7+1 = 22.

q: Rohan is 15th from the top in a class of 45 students. What is his rank from the bottom?
exp: Rank from bottom = 45−15+1 = 31.

q: In a row of 42 people, Sita is 11th from the left and Gita is 17th from the right. If Sita is to the left of Gita, how many people are between them?
exp: Gita's position from left = 42−17+1 = 26. People between = 26−11−1 = 14.

q: In a row of 60 students, Arjun is 24th from the left and Bharat is 19th from the right. If Arjun is to the left of Bharat, how many students are between them?
exp: Bharat's position from left = 60−19+1 = 42. Students between = 42−24−1 = 17.

q: In a class of 32 students, Mohan ranks 8th from the top. How many students are between the top position and Mohan?
exp: There are 7 students between the top position and Mohan's 8th position.

q: In a queue, P is 14th from the front and 21st from the back. How many people are in the queue?
Five students P, Q, R, S and T have different heights. P is taller than Q but shorter than R. S is shorter than Q but taller than T. Who is the tallest?
exp: R > P > Q > S > T. Therefore R is the tallest.

q: Among A, B, C, D and E, A is taller than B, B is taller than C, D is taller than A, and E is shorter than C. Who is the shortest?
exp: The order is D > A > B > C > E. Hence E is the shortest.

q: Six persons P, Q, R, S, T and U have different ages. P is older than Q but younger than R. S is younger than Q but older than T. U is older than R. Who is the oldest?
exp: The order is U > R > P > Q > S > T. Therefore U is oldest.

q: Five books A, B, C, D and E are arranged by price. A is costlier than B but cheaper than D. C is cheaper than B. E is costlier than D. Which book is the costliest?
exp: E > D > A > B > C. Therefore E is the costliest.

q: Among six runners, P finishes before Q but after R. S finishes after Q but before T. U finishes before R. Who finishes first?
exp: The order is U > R > P > Q > S > T in terms of finishing earlier. Thus U finishes first.

q: Seven students A, B, C, D, E, F and G stand in a line. A is to the left of B, C is to the right of B, D is to the left of A, E is to the right of C, F is between A and B, and G is to the left of D. Who is at the extreme left?
exp: The order begins G-D-A-F-B-C-E. Therefore G is at the extreme left.

q: Seven persons P, Q, R, S, T, U and V stand in a row. Q is to the right of P, R is to the right of Q, S is to the left of P, T is to the right of R, U is to the left of S, and V is between P and Q. Who is at the extreme right?
exp: The order is U-S-P-V-Q-R-T. Thus T is at the extreme right.

q: In a row of 31 people, Raj is 13th from the left and Simran is 9th from the right. If Raj is to the left of Simran, how many people stand between them?
exp: Simran's position from left = 31−9+1 = 23. People between = 23−13−1 = 9.

q: In a row of 45 people, A is 17th from the left and B is 12th from the right. How many people are between A and B if A is to the left of B?
exp: B's position from left = 45−12+1 = 34. Between = 34−17−1 = 16.

q: In a row of 36 students, Tina is 14th from the left and Mina is 11th from the right. How many students are between them if Tina is to the left of Mina?
exp: Mina's position from left = 36−11+1 = 26. Students between = 26−14−1 = 11.

q: A building has 12 floors numbered 1 to 12 from bottom to top. Rahul lives on the 5th floor. How many floors are above him?
exp: Floors above the 5th floor are 6 through 12: 7 floors.

q: In a building of 15 floors, Anu lives on the 9th floor from the bottom. What is her floor position from the top?
exp: Position from top = 15−9+1 = 7th.

q: A man lives on the 8th floor from the bottom of a building. If there are 5 floors above his floor, how many floors are in the building?
exp: Total floors = 8 + 5 = 13.

q: In a building of 20 floors, Riya's flat is on the 7th floor from the top. What is her floor number from the bottom?
exp: Floor from bottom = 20−7+1 = 14.

q: A building has 18 floors. P is on the 6th floor from the bottom, Q is on the 10th floor, and R is on the 15th floor. Who lives nearest to the top?
exp: The highest floor among the three is 15th, so R is nearest to the top.

q: In a class ranking, A ranks 7th, B ranks 12th, C ranks 18th, and D ranks 25th from the top. Who is ranked immediately after B among these students?
exp: The given ranks are 7, 12, 18 and 25. C is the next ranked student after B among these four.

q: Five candidates scored different marks. P scored more than Q but less than R. S scored less than Q but more than T. Who ranked second?
exp: The order is R > P > Q > S > T. Therefore P ranked second.

q: Six employees are ranked by performance. A is above B but below C. D is below B but above E. F is above C. Who ranks third?
exp: The order is F > C > A > B > D > E. Therefore A ranks third.

q: Eight students have ranks from 1 to 8. Ravi is ranked 3rd and Anil is ranked 7th. How many students are ranked between them?
exp: Students between ranks 3 and 7 are ranks 4, 5 and 6: 3 students.

q: In a competition of 100 participants, Meera ranks 18th. What percentage of participants rank below her?
exp: Participants below her = 100−18 = 82. Thus 82% rank below her.

q: In a group of 200 candidates, Arjun ranks 40th from the top. Approximately what percentile does he belong to, considering the percentage of candidates below him?
exp: Candidates below Arjun = 200−40 = 160, or 80% of the group. Thus he is approximately at the 80th percentile.

q: A student is ranked 25th out of 500 students. What percentage of students are ranked below him?
exp: Students below = 500−25 = 475. Percentage = 475/500×100 = 95%.

q: In a class of 80 students, Rohan is 20th from the top. What percentage of students rank above him?
exp: Students above = 19. Percentage = 19/80×100 = 23.75%.

q: Among 40 candidates, P ranks 12th, Q ranks 18th, and R ranks 25th from the top. What is the difference between P's and R's ranks?
exp: Difference = 25−12 = 13.

q: In a row of 25 people, A is 8th from the left and B is 10th from the right. If A and B exchange their positions, what will be A's new rank from the left?
exp: B's original position from left = 25−10+1 = 16. After exchanging positions, A becomes 16th from the left.

q: In a class of 50 students, Ravi ranks 15th from the top. If five students ranked above Ravi leave the class, what will be Ravi's new rank?
exp: Five students above Ravi leave, so his rank improves from 15th to 10th.

q: In a queue, P is 12th from the front. If 4 people ahead of P leave the queue, what will be P's new position?
exp: Four people ahead leave, so P moves from 12th to 8th.

q: In a row of 40 students, A is 11th from the left and B is 15th from the left. If 3 students between A and B leave the row, how many students will be between them?
exp: Originally, students between A and B = 15−11−1 = 3. If all 3 leave, no student remains between them.

q: Ten students P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W, X and Y have different ranks. P is above Q, Q is above R, S is below T but above U, V is above W, W is above X, and X is above Y. Which of the following must be true?
exp: P > Q > R is explicitly given. Therefore P must be above R.

q: Eight people have different heights. A is taller than B and C. D is taller than A but shorter than E. F is shorter than B but taller than G. H is shorter than C. Who is definitely taller than A?
exp: D is explicitly taller than A, while E is also taller than D. Therefore D is definitely taller than A.

q: In a ranking test, K is 9th from the top and 26th from the bottom. If three candidates join the test and are placed below K, what is K's new rank from the bottom?
exp: Originally 26 candidates are at or below K. Three new candidates join below K, so K's rank from bottom becomes 29th.
